chapters.title: Leadership: The Single Most Important Factor
chapters.sourcePressure: The introduction frames leadership quality as the factor that shapes whether teams perform, survive confusion, and adapt under pressure.
chapters.coreMove: turn uncertainty into a shared next action by naming the purpose, standard, and immediate move before conditions feel ready
chapters.commonMisread: leadership is important, so be more inspiring

chapters.title: Extreme Ownership
chapters.sourcePressure: The namesake chapter uses the Ramadi friendly-fire failure to show a leader refusing excuses and owning the system that produced the failure.
chapters.coreMove: accept responsibility at the level where repair becomes possible, then change the procedures and communication that shaped the result
chapters.commonMisread: take the blame publicly and move on

chapters.title: No Bad Teams, Only Bad Leaders
chapters.sourcePressure: The Hell Week boat-crew leader swap shows the same team performing differently when standards and leadership change.
chapters.coreMove: test the leader’s standard before judging the team by changing what the leader models, repeats, and accepts
chapters.commonMisread: bad teams do not exist, so leaders can magically fix anything

chapters.title: Believe
chapters.sourcePressure: Resistance to the Iraqi partner-force mission changes when leaders understand and explain why building partner capability matters.
chapters.coreMove: earn buy-in by understanding the mission deeply enough to explain its purpose without spin or borrowed language
chapters.commonMisread: make people believe by sounding confident

chapters.title: Check the Ego
chapters.sourcePressure: Elite-unit arrogance damages coordination, while humility and cross-unit respect return attention to the mission.
chapters.coreMove: notice when status protection is blocking help, correction, or cooperation, and put the mission back above looking right

chapters.title: Cover and Move
chapters.sourcePressure: Siloed units fail unless mutually dependent teams support one another as parts of one mission.
chapters.coreMove: find the adjacent team’s exposed point and support it while preserving clear ownership of the shared mission
chapters.commonMisread: teamwork means everyone helps everyone with everything

chapters.title: Simple
chapters.sourcePressure: Overcomplicated plans and explanations collapse under pressure; simple plans survive chaos because people can understand and execute them.
chapters.coreMove: compress the plan until the people under pressure can repeat the intent, sequence, and constraints from memory
chapters.commonMisread: simple means dumbed down or underplanned

chapters.title: Prioritize and Execute
chapters.sourcePressure: Leaders restore order in chaos by detaching, identifying the highest-priority problem, executing it, then reassessing.
chapters.coreMove: pause long enough to choose the controlling problem, act on it hard, then look up and choose again

chapters.title: Decentralized Command
chapters.sourcePressure: Leaders must train and trust junior leaders so decisions happen close to the facts instead of bottlenecking at the top.
chapters.coreMove: give local leaders intent, limits, and standards so they can decide without waiting for permission
chapters.commonMisread: delegate tasks and hope people figure it out

chapters.title: Plan
chapters.sourcePressure: Planning, commander’s intent, rehearsal, and contingency thinking improve adaptability under pressure.
chapters.coreMove: build a plan that gives people shared intent, roles, checks, and contingencies before pressure changes the route
chapters.commonMisread: make a detailed plan so uncertainty disappears

chapters.title: Leading Up and Down the Chain of Command
chapters.sourcePressure: Leaders must explain purpose down the chain and communicate friction proactively up the chain so aligned initiative can continue.
chapters.coreMove: move context down and reality up before people act from different maps

chapters.title: Decisiveness amid Uncertainty
chapters.sourcePressure: Leaders must make timely decisions with incomplete information, avoiding both hesitation and reckless speed.
chapters.coreMove: make a grounded call before perfect clarity arrives, then keep the team ready to revise as facts change
chapters.commonMisread: decisive leaders are certain and fast

chapters.title: Discipline Equals Freedom: The Dichotomy of Leadership
chapters.sourcePressure: Disciplined procedures create freedom of action, and leadership requires balancing tensions rather than choosing one extreme.
chapters.coreMove: use disciplined basics to free attention for judgment, then balance firmness with humility, speed with care, and control with trust
